summary:
MarsWalk is a prototype system for planning rover routes on Mars. It takes images of the Jezero crater acquired by the HiRISE camera and combines that with NASA's scientific data on Mars and very detailed terrain data to allow you to find a way to get from one point to another across the surface.

It uses four types of map data (elevation, slope, aspect and roughness) all derived from the HiRISE images. The map data is managed via a FastAPI application. Users of MarsWalk can view the terrain map, select a start and end point and then request a route. They can choose to find the shortest, safest or most scientifically interesting route. A path finding algorithm (A*) is used to examine the terrain, will avoid areas with no data and will provide the route with all the information necessary to compare the routes. There is also a catalogue of science data associated with particular locations which gives you some context about the environment but has no impact on the safety of the route.

MarsWalk was built using React, Python, FastAPI, QGIS, GDAL and Geotiff. It demonstrates how the analysis of map data and the ability to find paths subject to constraints can be of benefit in planning future Mars missions.
details:
MarsWalk is a terrain aware navigation platform which is used to plan rover routes across the surface of Mars. We're looking at the Jezero region and using real Mars terrain to go through the surface and find a path between two points.

The platform enables you to view a terrain map, select various map layers, pick your own starting point and destination. Once the points have been selected the backend will use an A* pathfinder to work out the route in three different modes: shortest, safest and science mode. It will take into account all the terrain attributes (slope, aspect, elevation, roughness etc) and will also check that the route you're going to take is within the valid data coverage. Any areas which are missing data are simply deemed to be out of bounds rather than being guessed at or interpolated. The resulting route is then shown on the map with all the associated route information (distance, terrain risk etc).

We built MarsWalk using real Mars data (HiRISE terrain and MOLA elevation data) and NASA science data (from Mastcam-Z and MEDA etc). The tech stack is React and Vite on the front end, Python and FastAPI on the back end, QGIS and GDAL for the geospatial processing, GeoTIFF for the terrain data and Git/Git LFS for version control and large file handling.

What sets MarsWalk apart is that it brings terrain visualisation, route planning and science related information into one package. It's not just about finding the shortest path, it's about taking into account the condition of the terrain and enabling the user to compare different route planning priorities. Our science aware mode provides a mechanism by which you can incorporate scientific interest as a factor whilst still having terrain condition as the primary consideration.

We've looked at terrain accuracy, data availability, coordinate systems, map alignment, missing data and the constraints of the Mars data sets we have available. We've also ensured that the system won't generate a route through terrain that we don't know about or that is invalid. The overall aim is to make Mars surface exploration a bit more accessible and to demonstrate how geospatial data and intelligent routing can assist in the safe and informed navigation of rovers on future Mars missions.
